examples.ko: 처음 만나는 자리에서 “처음 뵙겠습니다” 하고 인사해요.
examples.en: At a first meeting, I greet people with a formal “Nice to meet you”.
I went into the interview room and said “nice to meet you”.
I said “nice to meet you” to the department head and gave my business card.

examples.ko: 거래처 사람을 만나면 먼저 “처음 뵙겠습니다”라고 해요.
examples.en: When I meet a client, I first say “nice to meet you”.

examples.ko: “처음 뵙겠습니다”는 처음 만난 어른께 쓰는 인사예요.
examples.en: “Nice to meet you” in this formal form is a greeting for an elder you meet for the first time.

examples.ko: 저는 너무 긴장해서 “처음 뵙겠습니다”를 두 번 말했어요.
examples.en: I was so nervous that I said “nice to meet you” twice.

explain: 처음 만난 어른이나 격식 있는 자리에서 하는 인사예요. '뵙다'는 '보다'의 겸양 표현이라 윗사람에게 잘 어울려요. 또래나 편한 자리에서는 '안녕하세요, 만나서 반가워요'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: Hello, nice to meet you. I'm Suji.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural first greeting among peers or in relaxed settings.

phrases.en: Nice to meet you. I'm Minsu.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짧고 정중한 인사로, 처음 만난 자리에서 쓰기 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short, polite greeting that works well when meeting someone for the first time.

phrases.en: Nice to meet you. I am Suji Kim.
phrases.nuance_ko: 첫인사 뒤에 이름을 말할 때 격식 있게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal way to give your name right after the first greeting.

explain_en: This greeting is for elders or formal situations when you meet someone for the first time. '뵙다' is the humble form of '보다', so it suits people of higher status. With peers or in relaxed settings, '안녕하세요, 만나서 반가워요' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 처음 만난 사람에게 “만나서 반갑습니다” 하고 악수해요.
examples.en: I shake hands and say “nice to meet you” to someone I've just met.
Nice to meet you. I'm Suji.
At the interview, I greeted them first with “nice to meet you”.

examples.ko: 새 직장 동료들이 “만나서 반갑습니다” 하고 웃었어요.
examples.en: My new coworkers smiled and said “nice to meet you”.
Nice to meet you. Let's get along well from now on.

examples.ko: 외국 손님께 “만나서 반갑습니다”라고 한국말로 말해 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried saying “nice to meet you” in Korean to a foreign guest.

explain: 처음 만났을 때 쓰는 정중한 인사로, 보통 '안녕하세요' 다음에 말해요. 조금 더 부드럽고 편하게 하려면 '만나서 반가워요'라고 해요. 이미 아는 사람에게는 '오랜만이에요'를 써요.

phrases.en: Nice to meet you. I'm Jiwoo.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 부드럽고 편한 말투예요. 친구나 동료에게 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer, more relaxed tone that suits friends and coworkers.

phrases.en: Nice to meet you. I'm Jiwoo.
phrases.nuance_en: Casual speech for peers or children.

phrases.en: Nice to meet you too. I look forward to working with you.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대가 먼저 인사했을 때 대답으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A reply to use when the other person greeted you first.

explain_en: This is a polite greeting for a first meeting, usually said right after '안녕하세요'. For a softer, more relaxed tone, say '만나서 반가워요'. For someone you already know, use '오랜만이에요' instead.

en: Please take care of me / I look forward to working with you

examples.en: I bowed my head and said “I look forward to working with you”.

examples.ko: 첫 출근 날 팀원들에게 “잘 부탁드립니다” 하고 말했어요.
examples.en: On my first day at work, I said “please take care of me” to my team.

examples.ko: 잘 부탁드립니다. 저는 오늘부터 여기서 일해요.
examples.en: Nice to be working with you. I start working here today.

examples.ko: 이사 온 이웃에게 “앞으로 잘 부탁드립니다”라고 인사했어요.
examples.en: I greeted my new neighbors with “please look after me from now on”.

examples.ko: 처음 뵙겠습니다. 잘 부탁드립니다. 저는 민수예요.
examples.en: Nice to meet you. I look forward to working with you. I'm Minsu.

examples.ko: 일을 맡길 때 “잘 부탁드립니다”를 쓰면 정중해요.
examples.en: Saying a polite “Please take care of this” when you hand over a task sounds respectful.

explain: 영어로 딱 맞는 말이 없어요. 상황에 따라 '앞으로 잘 부탁해요', '잘 돌봐 주세요', '믿고 맡길게요' 같은 느낌이에요. 처음 만난 자리의 인사로도 쓰고, 일을 맡기면서 부탁할 때도 써요. 친구에게는 '잘 부탁해'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Please take care of me from now on.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동료나 또래에게 편하게 하는 말이에요. 어른께는 '잘 부탁드립니다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A relaxed version for coworkers or peers. Use the formal version with elders.

phrases.example: 잘 부탁해! 우리 같이 열심히 하자.
phrases.en: Please take care of me! Let's work hard together.
Please help me out. This is my first time.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite but softer-sounding than the formal version.
phrases.en_equiv: I look forward to it (soft, polite)

explain_en: There is no exact English match; depending on the situation it feels like 'let's get along', 'please look after me', or 'I'm counting on you'. It is used both as a greeting at a first meeting and when entrusting someone with a task. With friends, you say '잘 부탁해'.

examples.en: Excuse me, may I have your name?
You made a reservation, right? May I have your name?

examples.ko: 병원 접수처 직원이 “성함이 어떻게 되세요?” 하고 물었어요.
examples.en: The hospital reception staff asked, “May I have your name?”

examples.ko: 전화로 주문하실 때 성함이 어떻게 되세요?
examples.en: When you order by phone, may I have your name?

examples.ko: 처음 오셨네요. 손님, 성함이 어떻게 되세요?
examples.en: It's your first visit. Customer, may I have your name?

examples.ko: 택배를 받으시는 분 성함이 어떻게 되세요?
examples.en: May I have the name of the person receiving the package?

explain: '이름이 뭐예요?'보다 훨씬 공손해서 손님이나 어른의 이름을 물을 때 써요. '성함'은 남의 이름을 높이는 말이라 내 이름을 말할 때는 쓰지 않고 '이름'이나 '저는 ~예요'라고 해요. 병원, 가게, 전화 응대에서 자주 들어요.

phrases.en: Is this your first visit? May I have your name?
phrases.nuance_ko: '되세요'보다 더 격식 있는 말이라 회사나 공식 자리에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: More formal than '되세요', for work or official settings.

phrases.en: Could you tell me your name?
phrases.nuance_en: A soft way to ask someone for their name.
phrases.en_equiv: could you tell me your name

phrases.nuance_ko: '성함'보다 쉽고 덜 공손해서 또래나 아이에게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and less polite than '성함', for peers or children.

explain_en: It is far more polite than '이름이 뭐예요?', so you use it to ask a customer's or elder's name. '성함' is the honorific for someone else's name, so you never use it for your own; say '이름' or '저는 ~예요'. You often hear it at hospitals, shops and on the phone.

examples.en: Yesterday I met my friend after a long time.
On the weekend I cooked at home for the first time in a while.
Going back to my hometown after a long time, it had changed a lot.
Oh my, it's been a long time! Have you been well?
On Sunday I slept in for the first time in a long while.
I watched a movie for the first time in ages and it was really fun.

explain: 인사로는 '오랜만이에요'라고 하고, 어떤 일을 오래 못 하다가 했을 때는 '오랜만에'를 써요. '오래간만에'가 원래 말이고 '오랜만에'는 그 줄임말이에요.

phrases.en: I went on a trip with my family after a long time.
phrases.nuance_en: The original form of the headword, with the same meaning.

phrases.en: Long time no see! How have you been?
phrases.nuance_ko: 오랫동안 못 만난 사람에게 하는 인사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A greeting for someone you haven't seen in a long time.

phrases.en: It was a rare day off, so I slept in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오랜만에 생긴 좋은 기회나 시간을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a rare good chance or time that finally came.

explain_en: As a greeting you say '오랜만이에요' (long time no see), and '오랜만에' is used when you do something after not doing it for a long time. '오래간만에' is the original form and '오랜만에' is its shortened version.

examples.en: What's your friend's name?
This isn't my name.
What's your name? — I'm Haruka.
I write my name on the paper.
This café has a pretty name.

explain: 어른에게는 '이름' 대신 '성함'을 써요: '성함이 어떻게 되세요?' 그리고 한국어는 성(김, 이, 박)이 먼저, 이름이 뒤예요. 이름만 부르는 건 친한 사이에서만 해요.

phrases.en: to live up to one's name/reputation
phrases.nuance_en: a compliment when something is as good as expected
phrases.en_equiv: to live up to one's name/reputation

phrases.example: 이름도 성도 모르는 사람이 돈을 빌려 달래요.
phrases.en: to not know someone at all
phrases.nuance_en: stresses that you don't know the person at all
phrases.en_equiv: to not know someone at all

explain_en: For elders, use the honorific 성함 instead of 이름: 성함이 어떻게 되세요? ('May I ask your name?'). Korean names put the family name (Kim, Lee, Park) first. Calling someone by given name alone is only for close relationships.

dis.h: Everyday word for names, including people

p.n: 명칭 is more formal and used only for things or organizations.

en: nice to meet you (at a first meeting)
usage: 만나서 반가워요 = full greeting at a first meeting. 반가워요 alone also works.

examples.en: I'm Louis. Nice to meet you.
Hello, I'm a doctor. Nice to meet you.
This is my friend. — Oh, nice to meet you.
I'm German. Nice to meet you.
Nice to meet you too.

explain: 만나서 반가워요는 처음 만난 사람에게 해요. 다시 만났을 때는 “반가워요”라고 해요. 대답은 “저도요”가 편해요.
explain_en: Say 만나서 반가워요 to someone you meet for the first time. When you meet again, just say 반가워요. An easy reply is 저도요 (“me too”).

examples.ko: 중의성이 있는 문장은 쉼표 하나로도 뜻이 갈린다.
examples.en: In a sentence with ambiguity, even one comma can split the meaning.

examples.ko: '예쁜 친구의 동생'은 누가 예쁜지 알 수 없어서 중의성이 있어요.
examples.en: "The younger sibling of my pretty friend" is ambiguous because you can't tell who is pretty.

examples.ko: 계약서의 중의성은 분쟁으로 이어질 수 있어서 반드시 없애야 합니다.
examples.en: Ambiguity in a contract can lead to disputes, so it must be removed.

examples.ko: 중의성을 줄이려고 주어를 문장 앞에 분명히 적었어요.
examples.en: To reduce ambiguity, I wrote the subject clearly at the start of the sentence.

examples.ko: 광고 문구의 중의성 때문에 소비자 항의가 들어왔습니다.
examples.en: Complaints from consumers came in because of the ambiguity of the ad copy.

explain: 중의성은 문장이 둘 이상의 뜻으로 읽힐 때 써요. '중의적인 표현'이라고도 해요. 어순을 바꾸거나 주어를 밝히면 줄일 수 있어요.
explain_en: 중의성 is used when a sentence can be read in two or more ways; people also say 중의적인 표현. You can reduce it by changing the word order or stating the subject.

examples.ko: 논문 작성법 특강은 대학원생이면 누구나 들을 수 있다.
examples.en: Any graduate student can attend the special lecture on how to write a thesis.

examples.ko: 오늘 오후에 취업 준비 특강이 있어서 강의실이 가득 찼어요.
examples.en: There was a special lecture on job preparation this afternoon, so the lecture hall was full.

examples.ko: 선배가 졸업생 특강에서 회사 생활에 대해 이야기해 줬어요.
examples.en: A senior talked about working life at the alumni special lecture.

examples.ko: 방학 동안 영어 회화 특강을 들으려고 학원에 등록했어요.
examples.en: I registered at an academy to take an English conversation special course during vacation.

examples.ko: 이번 특강에서는 발표 자료를 만드는 방법을 알려 줍니다.
examples.en: This special lecture will show you how to make presentation materials.

explain: '특별 강의'를 줄인 말로, 정규 수업 밖에서 열려요. 앞에 '초청 특강', '방학 특강'처럼 누가 하는지, 언제 하는지를 붙여 말해요.

dict_examples.ko: 학교에서는 여름 방학 동안 글짓기 특강을 개설한다.
dict_examples.en: The school will open a special writing lecture during summer vacation.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: It's short for 특별 강의 (special lecture) and takes place outside the regular timetable. People put who or when in front: '초청 특강' (guest lecture), '방학 특강' (vacation course).

examples.en: Long time no see. How have you been?
I went back to my hometown for the first time in ages.
It rained for the first time in a while, so it's cool.
Yesterday I slept in for the first time in a while.

examples.ko: 오래간만이에요! 요즘 어디에서 일해요? — 지금은 부산에서 일해요.
examples.en: Long time no see! Where do you work these days? — I work in Busan now.

explain: 오랜만은 오래간만의 줄임말이에요. 말할 때는 “오랜만이에요”를 더 많이 써요. 친구에게는 “오랜만이야”라고 해요.

dict_examples.en: I met an old friend after a long time.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: It rained for the first time in a long while.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 오래간만에 가 본 고향은 참으로 많이 변해 있었다.
dict_examples.en: My hometown, which I visited after a long time, had changed a lot.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 오랜만 is the short form of 오래간만, and it is what people mostly say. With friends, use 오랜만이야.

dis.h: full, longer form of 'after a while'

p.n: Same meaning; 오랜만 is shorter and more common.
